newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Saxony state plans tight '98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Saxony state plans tight '98 budget.

text.p: The east German federal state of Saxony plans to tighten up borrowing next year under a budget adopted by Christian Democrat (CDU) premier Kurt Biedenkopf's cabinet on Tuesday.

According to the budget plan, the deficit would fall by 290 million marks to 1.1 billion marks, while the state would keep the highest ratio of investment to spending among Germany's 16 federal states, Finance Minister Georg Milbradt said.
Milbradt added that under a medium-term plan the number of state employees would be reduced by 13,000 by the year 2002 from 111,000 now.

New borrowing by federal states and municipalities makes up around half of the total public sector deficit, which federal Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to get below three percent of gross domestic product both this year and next to qualify for Europe's single currency.
